> 第61章 离开（第1页）

这七天里，他没有闲着。第一天，他帮李神医把医馆里所有库存的药材重新分类、标注，按“凡人可用”和“修士专用”分成两套药柜。第二天，他帮王屠户把村口案板修理了一遍——案板中间那道被斩骨刀劈出的深槽已经影响使用了，两人用刨子刨平、抹上桐油、晾了一整天。第三天，他帮赵伯整理了院子里堆积多年的杂物，在一口旧木箱里翻出了一摞泛黄的信札，赵伯接过去翻了翻，沉默了很久，然后锁进了柜子里。第四天到第六天，他劈柴、巡村、给孙老六复查，把防疫巡查的要点写在纸上交给药童，反复叮嘱他每日换药、每日巡查水源，一个字一个字地教他辨认水质异常的特征。
他没有刻意道别。老陆、王屠户、赵伯、李神医也没有刻意送他。在青山村，告别是一件不需要仪式的事——活得久了，见惯了离别，仪式反而成了负担。
第七天清晨，秦川背着一个粗布包袱，站在村口的老槐树下。苏木槿牵着她那匹青骢马等在路边，马背上已经驮着一个装药草标本的竹篓。她今天没有穿圣女的白裙，换成了一身淡青色的布衣，长发用木簪挽在脑后，看起来倒像个普通的采药女。
秦川没有骑马，也没有准备干粮。他从老陆的柴堆里捡了一块劈好的柴，塞进包袱里——很轻，很糙，断面还有斧刃留下的纹理。他也不确定自己为什么这么做，也许只是想在离开的时候，带上一件能让他想起劈柴声的东西。
秦川回头看了一眼村子。晨光中，青山村和往常一样安静。老槐树下的石桌上空着，棋篓里的黑白棋子还在，仿佛赵伯只是起身去烧水了。村口的案板上干干净净，王屠户的斩骨刀插在案板边上，刀刃上还挂着水珠——刚用井水冲洗过。医馆的门半掩着，药童正蹲在门口捣药，石臼里发出有节奏的笃笃声，和老陆的劈柴声很像。
老陆的院子里没有劈柴声。院门开着，劈柴男人坐在石墩上，手里握着那把重新蒙上铁锈的柴斧。左臂的绷带已经拆了，伤口结了痂，但握斧头的姿势还是只用右手，看上去和平日没什么不同。
秦川走到院门口，站住。老陆抬眼看了他一下。“走了？”
“中界比青山村复杂。百草谷不是世外桃源，外面有外面的规矩。”老陆低头看着手里的柴斧，像是在跟斧头说话，“但你是劈柴的。劈柴的人不管柴有多硬、有多少节疤，只问斧刃够不够利、手够不够稳。”
他顿了顿：“你的斧头，够利了。”
秦川没有说话。老陆将柴斧放在膝上，抬头看着他。“记住一件事——不管中界的人跟你说什么、给你什么、许诺什么，你终究是青山村的人。轮回剑的记名弟子，不是好当的。但你是自己选的。自己选的，就不要后悔。”
老陆点了点头，然后站起来，走到秦川面前，将一样东西放进他手里。不是剑穗，不是铁签。是一块磨刀石。很小，只有半个巴掌大，粗砺的表面上有一道道深浅不一的凹痕——那是他磨剑时留下的痕迹。
“中界没有劈柴的地方。但你每天要磨刀。”劈柴男人说，“磨刀的人，不会忘了劈柴的人。”
秦川将磨刀石放进怀里，点了点头。他转身走出院门，走过村口的老槐树，走过井边那块被磨得光滑的石板，走过隔离室门口堆放的新柴。走到村道拐弯处时，他停了一下，回头看了一眼。
没有人在村口送他。但劈柴声重新响起来了。笃、笃、笃。节奏很稳，和在青山村的每一天一样。他知道那是老陆在告诉他：村子还在。劈柴还在。你走，我不送。你回来，我还在这里劈柴。
秦川转回头，跟着苏木槿踏上了通往中界的山道。

> Chapter 61 Leaving (Page 1)
During these seven days, he was not idle. On the first day, he helped Divine Doctor Li reclassify and label all the medicinal materials in stock in the medical clinic, and divided them into two sets of medicine cabinets according to "for mortals" and "for monks only". The next day, he helped Butcher Wang repair the chopping board at the entrance of the village - the deep groove in the middle of the chopping board that had been cut by the bone-chopping knife had affected its use. The two of them used a plane to smooth it out, apply tung oil and let it dry for a whole day. On the third day, he helped Uncle Zhao sort out the debris that had accumulated in the yard for many years, and found a pile of yellowed letters in an old wooden box. Uncle Zhao took it and flipped through it. He was silent for a long time, and then locked it in the cabinet. From the fourth to the sixth day, he chopped firewood, patrolled the village, and rechecked Sun Laoliu. He wrote down the key points of the epidemic prevention inspection on paper and gave it to the medicine boy. He repeatedly told him to change the dressing every day, inspect the water source every day, and taught him word by word to identify the characteristics of abnormal water quality.
He didn't mean to say goodbye. Lao Lu, Butcher Wang, Uncle Zhao, and Divine Doctor Li didn't send him away deliberately. In Qingshan Village, farewell is something that does not require a ceremony - after living for a long time and getting used to farewells, rituals have become a burden.
In the early morning of the seventh day, Qin Chuan stood under the old locust tree at the entrance of the village, carrying a coarse cloth bundle. Su Mujin was waiting by the roadside with her green horse, which already carried a bamboo basket containing medicinal herb specimens on its back. She did not wear the white dress of the saint today, but changed into a light blue cloth. Her long hair was tied back with a wooden hairpin. She looked like an ordinary herb picking girl.
Qin Chuan did not ride a horse and did not prepare dry food. He picked up a piece of chopped firewood from Lao Lu's firewood pile and stuffed it into his baggage - it was very light and rough, and the cross section still had the texture left by the ax blade. He wasn't sure why he did this, maybe he just wanted to take something that reminded him of the sound of chopping wood when he left.
Qin Chuan looked back at the village. In the morning light, Qingshan Village was as quiet as usual. The stone table under the old locust tree was empty, and the black and white chess pieces in the chess basket were still there, as if Uncle Zhao just got up to boil water. The chopping board at the entrance of the village was clean. Butcher Wang's bone-chopping knife was stuck on the edge of the chopping board. There were still water droplets hanging on the blade - it had just been rinsed with well water. The door of the medical center was ajar, and the medicine boy was squatting at the door pounding medicine. The stone mortar made a rhythmic click sound, which was very similar to the sound of Lao Lu chopping firewood.
There was no sound of wood chopping in Lao Lu's yard. The courtyard door was open, and the man chopping firewood was sitting on the stone pier, holding the wood ax that had been covered with rust again in his hand. The bandage on his left arm has been removed and the wound has scabbed over, but he still holds the ax with his right hand, looking no different from usual.
Qin Chuan walked to the entrance of the courtyard and stopped. Lao Lu looked up at him. "Leaving?"
"The middle world is more complicated than Qingshan Village. Baicao Valley is not a paradise, and there are rules outside." Old Lu looked down at the firewood ax in his hand, as if talking to the axe, "But you are a firewood chopper. People who chop firewood don't care how hard the firewood is or how many knots there are, they only ask whether the ax blade is sharp enough and the hand is stable enough."
He paused: "Your ax is sharp enough."
Qin Chuan said nothing. Lao Lu put the wood ax on his knees and looked up at him. "Remember one thing - no matter what the people in the middle world tell you, give you, or promise you, you are still from Qingshan Village after all. It is not easy to be a registered disciple of the Samsara Sword. But you chose it yourself. If you choose it, don't regret it."
Lao Lu nodded, then stood up, walked to Qin Chuan, and put something into his hand. Not a sword spike, not an iron sign. It's a whetstone. It was very small, only half the size of a palm, and there were dents of varying depths on the rough surface - the marks left when he sharpened his sword.
"There is no place to chop wood in the middle world. But you have to sharpen the knife every day." The man chopping wood said, "The person who sharpens the knife will never forget the person who chops wood."
Qin Chuan put the whetstone into his arms and nodded. He turned around and walked out of the courtyard, walking past the old locust tree at the entrance of the village, past the polished stone slab beside the well, and past the new firewood piled at the door of the isolation room. When he reached the corner of the village road, he paused and looked back.
No one saw him off at the entrance of the village. But the sound of chopping wood started again. Dude, dunk, dunk. The rhythm is very steady, just like every day in Qingshan Village. He knew that it was Lao Lu telling him: the village is still there. The firewood is still being chopped. You leave, I won’t send you away. When you come back, I'll still be chopping firewood here.
Qin Chuan turned around and followed Su Muxin on the mountain road leading to the middle realm.
